mainText: This is Dose of Good for Friday, November 20. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Potiguara Indigenous farmers bring in their first agroecological cotton harvest. In Paraíba, Brazil, families in the Potiguara Indigenous Territory harvested cotton grown alongside peanuts and beans, with no chemicals. The Embrapa-backed project trained growers, the association bought a tractor, and plots will expand next season. Second: Giant anteater returns to an Argentine reserve after almost 40 years. At the Alma Guaraní reserve in the Chaco, volunteers have been restoring the forest for over a decade. Camera traps caught a giant anteater, the first since 1986, mostly in areas left to regrow naturally. Third: Indigenous-designed desert home wins an Australian innovation award. The Explain Home, designed by Warumungu man Norman Frank Jupurrurla and Serina Morton, has verandahs, breezeways, an outdoor kitchen and solar power to tackle overcrowding and extreme heat. A 20-home project is under discussion. Fourth: Polar permafrost fungi could become natural herbicides. UFMG researchers are screening fungi from frozen soils in Greenland and Antarctica for compounds that stop weeds. Their lab holds a collection of more than 20,000 strains. Fifth: Viagra-family pill slows memory loss in early Alzheimer's. In a Phase 3 trial, AR1001 slowed cognitive decline by 31% in 604 people with early Alzheimer's who weren't on other drugs. Results are topline, and experts call for more research. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
